definitions.meaning: to cut into a conversation or proceedings
a forced entry into a building to steal

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the phrase means to cut into talk; as a noun it is a forced entry by a thief.

definitions.meaning: to pound or bombard hard and repeatedly
the hide of a beast with its fur on

explanation.definitionFit: To pelt is to hammer away at something; a pelt is also a hide with the fur still attached.

definitions.meaning: an informal, everyday word for a glance

explanation.surface: A bird with an ordinary appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The male goose shares its name with slang for a quick glance, as in 'take a gander'.

indicators.note: having problems suggests the word recounts is thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone patiently sets out what went wrong with vote recounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems with' tells you to rearrange the letters of RECOUNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret or analyse the meaning of words with care.

parts.note: quick in the old sense means alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'
a wage is money paid for work

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is fast cash, and is told it is only a modest income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like it means fast, but here it carries its old sense of alive, giving LIVING.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay level just sufficient to meet basic costs of life is a small, adequate income.

clue.text: Senior lawyer presents magistrates to monarch

parts.note: the bench is the collective term for magistrates or judges
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A lawyer introduces the magistrates to the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: BENCH is the collective term for magistrates; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a bencher is a senior member governing one of the Inns of Court.

clue.text: Paths the artillery have taken back to weapon store

indicators.note: being taken back means the combined letters are read from end to start

parts.note: lanes are narrow paths or tracks
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Gunners retreat along the tracks to their armoury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns the whole run LANESRA round, so it reads from the end. RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a depot where arms and ammunition are kept.

clue.text: Have consultations about one type of tree

indicators.note: about means the word for consulting goes around the numeral

parts.note: to confer is to talk things over together
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: People hold talks concerning a particular kind of tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CONFER around I, the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pines, firs and spruces are cone-bearing evergreens, a whole class of trees.

clue.text: Fighter taking to the air in Chinese rebellion

parts.note: a boxer fights in the ring
rising means going up into the sky

explanation.surface: A fighter takes to the skies during an uprising in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boxer Rising, or Boxer Rebellion, was the anti-foreign uprising in China around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic revolt of 1899 to 1901 led by a Chinese secret society is known by this name.

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so these letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: Someone fussy complains that the studio is untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' says to rearrange IF, STUDIOS and A, keeping the S of the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastidious person is fussy and hard to please about details.

clue.text: Restless desire to see small Italian church

parts.note: IT is the short form of Italian

explanation.surface: A traveller longs to visit a little church in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a nagging urge or craving for something.

clue.text: Gone With The Wind broadcast to most of Borneo

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it except its final letter, here the island's name

explanation.surface: The classic film is being shown to viewers across much of Borneo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone With The Wind' looks like the film title but is the definition. 'most of' drops the last O of Borneo, leaving BORNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried off by moving air is flying, aloft on the breeze.

clue.text: Trouble is, I need replacement work clothes

indicators.note: needing replacement suggests the letters of these words are to be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains their workwear is wrecked and must be renewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need replacement' rearranges TROUBLE, IS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler suit is a one-piece overall worn for manual jobs.

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked for their shabby clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to tease them; clothes that are torn and frayed are also described this way.

parts.note: seems to ask about a prize for a holiday house, but means the prize given to the runner-up who comes home in second place

explanation.surface: A prize for owning a holiday cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second home' suggests a country cottage, but means finishing a race in second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up in an Olympic event receives a medal of the second most precious metal.

clue.text: Coming to see bomb requires careful placing

parts.note: the V1 flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI
siting is the choosing of a position for something

explanation.surface: A visitor learns that a bomb must be positioned with care.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 was a German flying bomb; written with a Roman-looking I it gives VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying a call on someone means going to see them.

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
to net is to catch and secure

explanation.surface: A person hails a taxi to collect government ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers of a government form a committee known by this name.

clue.text: Jog being finished, get hit by car

parts.note: to jog is to run gently
over means ended

explanation.surface: A jogger's outing ends with being struck by a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knocked down by a vehicle is to be run over; the definition stands for the passive phrase.

indicators.note: about means the word for worries goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: cares are worries

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a second blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CARES around S (second), between its E and final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroke someone gently and fondly is to touch them lovingly.

parts.note: a share is a stake held as an investment in a company
out means left out or excluded

explanation.surface: Gamblers split the pot, leaving the stake money out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: a dividing-up of winnings, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A distribution of money or goods among a group is a division of spoils.

clue.text: Muslim leader about to conclude business programme

indicators.note: about means the leader's title goes around the word for finishing

parts.note: an aga is a Muslim commander or chief
to end is to conclude

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader is about to wrap up the meeting's business.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'about to' as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal, wrapping the Muslim title round the word for finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting is its running order.

definitions.meaning: to not catch or not hit

explanation.surface: Someone does not manage to win a girl's affections.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall short of hitting a target, and the title for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: For recruit, not to defer is dreadful

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad state, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: For a new army recruit, delaying service is terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' says to rearrange NOT TO DEFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or novice.

indicators.note: ill suggests the letters of feel are in poor order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels sick and rushes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run off quickly from danger.

clue.text: Fainted, being ordered to be rebellious

indicators.note: being put in order means the letters of fainted are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed when told to rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A defiant person openly resists authority.

indicators.note: held means the word for adding surrounds the word for being in attendance

parts.note: to tot up is to add
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A small child clutched a gift tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but means add up, and 'present' looks like a gift but means in attendance; 'held' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick firmly to something is to cling on tightly.
